title: Region-First Routing Lab: Console Policy DSL + Live Simulation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Console-first experience that lets customers author and validate multi-dimensional routing policies focused on region selection, tier routing (Dedicated/Hosted), and automatic fallback to model variants. Deliver a lightweight policy DSL editor alongside a live simulation canvas that runs representative request traces and cost/latency projections. The goal is to reduce operator errors when configuring fallbacks, make region-priority behavior explicit, and provide safe defaults for cost-sensitive workloads.
user_stories: As a platform engineer I want to define region-priority lists with per-region weight and tier constraints so traffic follows predictable locality and SLA rules.
As an app owner I want policies to fall back to cheaper quantized model variants automatically when preferred capacity is unavailable so my feature stays online without manual intervention.
As an SRE I want a validation step that flags unsafe fallbacks (e.g., cross-region data egress or model variants with known quality regressions) to avoid incidents.
As a QA engineer I want to run a live simulation with synthetic request traces and see latency/cost projections before saving a policy.
acceptance_criteria: Console includes a new 'Routing Lab' tab where users can author policies using the DSL and the visual preview.
Policy DSL supports region lists with priority/weight, tier selectors (hosted,dedicated,private), and fallback chains pointing at model variants with version pins.
Validation rules run on save and surface blocking errors and non-blocking warnings (e.g., potential data egress, high cost estimates).

Simulation runs against a customer-configurable trace (sampled or custom) and shows: expected p50/p95 latency, estimated per-token cost, and % of requests that will hit each model variant by default and under failure scenarios.
Support for canary splits (e.g., 5% to fallback variant) in the simulator and ability to export a JSON policy to API or infra config.
Docs and a short in-console walkthrough are published alongside the feature (Confluence + Console help panel).
